evidence_scope_projection.definition: Overall prostate cancer evidence, excluding estimates solely about aggressive prostate cancer. General estimates from papers that also report aggressive endpoints remain included. Uncertain endpoints retain their existing review and pooling restrictions.

headline.funnel_interpretation: Egger’s test is generally not recommended when fewer than 10 studies are available.
headline.results_interpretation: The pooled analysis of 2 studies yielded an overall effect size of 0.73 (95% CI: 0.58–0.92), suggesting that Vitamin K is associated with a lower risk of prostate cancer\aggressive. These findings were supported by low between-study heterogeneity (I² = 0.00%), indicating consistent findings across the included studies.

cases.excerpt: In this nested case-control study including 250 prostate cancer cases and 494 matched controls, we aimed to confirm this cancer-protective effect using serum undercarboxylated osteocalcin (ucOC), a biomarker of vitamin K status inversely associated with vitamin K intake.

confidence_interval.excerpt: Serum ucOC/iOC ratio was positively associated with advanced-stage (OR per 0.1 increment, 1.38; 95% CI, 1.03-1.86) and high-grade prostate cancer (OR, 1.21; 95% CI, 1.00-1.46) but not with total prostate cancer.

The significant association with advanced-stage prostate cancer was confirmed when serum ucOC/iOC ratio was jointly modeled with menaquinone intake data.
